title: Subak settings, config_version 1 (the data model of config.toml)
description: The settings of %APPDATA%\mouv\subak\config.toml (Step 20, ADR 0051, docs/SUBAK_GUI.md §13, docs/contracts/STATE_SCHEMA.md §2) as JSON: the file is TOML, and `subak config show --json` reports these values as `settings` (every key with its effective value). Display and behaviour settings of the Subak window and basic local shell profiles only: no process ids, terminal content or secrets. Unknown keys are allowed in the file and kept by every edit; an invalid value falls back to its default alone. Profile values shown by Subak are redacted (`***`) where they look secret.

theme.description: auto: kim-dark, or the system colours while Windows High Contrast is on. system: kim-light while Windows apps use the light mode, else kim-dark (High Contrast wins). kim-dark, kim-light: always. high-contrast: the system colours always.

font_family.description: The terminal font family tried first; the design system's chain (Cascadia Mono, Consolas, D2Coding, Malgun Gothic, Segoe UI Emoji, Segoe UI Symbol) follows it. Empty: the chain alone.

font_size.description: Terminal text size in logical pixels (size.terminal, default 13); the zoom keys change it.

line_height.description: The cell height as a multiple of the text size (line-height.terminal, default 1.2).

padding.description: Logical pixels around the cell grid (default 8).

opacity.description: Window opacity in percent (default 100). High Contrast always draws opaque.

motion.description: system: follow Windows' Show animations setting; reduced: no motion; full: short transitions always.

minimum_contrast.description: #98 T4: the least contrast of text against its background (WCAG ratio); text below it is moved toward white or black. 1.0 turns it off; default 4.5 (KIM-NFR-012).

density.description: #98 T1: regular (default) or compact (a lower tab bar).

bold_is_bright.description: Bold text in ANSI colours 0-7 uses the bright variants (default true).

close_buttons.description: Each tab has its x (hide) button (default true; pinned tabs never do).

cycle.description: The next/previous tab keys wrap around at the ends (default true).

title.description: #98 T1: what a tab shows: {name} (default), {title} (set by the program), {program}, {cwd} (folder name), with any text around them.

on_exit.description: #98 T1: when the shown tab's program ends: keep (default, its last screen stays) or close.

height.description: Its height in percent of the monitor's work area (default 40).

hide_on_blur.description: It hides when another window gets the focus (default true); gui.show brings it back.

default_profile.description: The profile Ctrl+T, + and `subak new` (without a program) start; empty: the Host's default shell.

copy_on_select.description: A mouse selection is copied when the button is released (default false).

claude_indicators.description: Step 28: tabs and the title show each Terminal's Claude Code state from hooks (default true).

claude_animation.description: Step 44: the Claude marks move (default true); false or reduced motion: static marks, no timer.

detect_shells.description: Step 33: the shells found on this PC (PowerShell 7, Windows PowerShell, Command Prompt, Git Bash, since #98 T4 Command Prompt with Clink, Cygwin, MSYS2 environments, Cmder and the Visual Studio developer prompts, and WSL distributions) are offered as profiles (default true).

smart_ctrl_c.description: Ctrl+C copies when text is selected, else it reaches the program (default false).

alt_is_meta.description: #98 T2: Alt with a character sends ESC first (default true, as in Windows Terminal); false: the character alone.

notify_command_seconds.description: #98 T3: a notification when a shell-integration command (OSC 133) that ran at least this many seconds finishes while its tab is not shown or the window is not in front; 0 (default): never.

pane_labels.description: #98 T1: a split window labels each pane with its index and program (default false).

focus_follows_mouse.description: #98 T1: pointing at another pane of a split window makes it the active one (default false).

notify_exit.description: #98 T3: a notification when a Terminal's program ends while its tab is not shown or the window is not in front (default false).

bell.description: #98 T3: what a bell in the shown pane does: off (default), visual (the pane flashes; the taskbar button too while the window is not in front) or audible (the system sound and the visual bell).

backspace.description: #98 T2: what Backspace sends: del (DEL 0x7F, default), ctrl-h (BS 0x08) or delete (CSI 3 ~).

right_click.description: copy-paste (default): copy a selection, else paste; menu: the pane menu; paste; none.

word_separators.description: Characters that end a word for double-click selection and mark mode.

repeat_time_ms.description: Step 23, tmux repeat-time: milliseconds after a repeatable prefix key (Ctrl+B Ctrl+Arrow) during which it works again without the prefix; 0 turns that off (default 500).

highlights.description: #98 T4: keyword rules the window draws: text matching pattern (a regular expression) in color.

color.description: red, orange, yellow, green, teal, blue, purple, pink or #rrggbb.

quick_commands.description: #98 T4: saved snippets the window sends as input (palette: to this tab or to every tab).

profiles.description: Basic local shell profiles ([[profiles]] in the file). SSH and other profile kinds are Step 33.

program.description: A program path, or a bare name looked up on the pane's PATH; never run through a shell.

cwd.description: An absolute working directory; absent or null: the Host's default (the user's profile folder).

env.description: Variables set in the pane (names as env_name). Values that look secret are shown as ***; Subak never writes them.

title.description: Step 33: the name a new Terminal of this profile gets when none is given and it is free.

ssh.description: Step 34 (ADR 0067): an SSH profile's destination `[user@]host[:port]` instead of `program`/`args`; the pane runs Windows' OpenSSH client. Never a secret.

identity.description: Step 34: an SSH profile's private key file (absolute; `ssh -i`).

jump.description: Step 35 (ADR 0068): an SSH profile's jump hosts, in order (`[user@]host[:port]`; ProxyJump).

forwards.description: Step 35: an SSH profile's port forwards (`L:port:host:port`, `R:…`, `D:port`); they listen on loopback only.

agent_forward.description: Step 35: forward the SSH agent (off unless set; every connection warns about it).

group.description: Step 36 (ADR 0069): the group the profile is listed under; detected shells are in `Detected`.

login_script.description: Step 35: an SSH profile's login script (absolute path; `[[step]] expect`/`send`, never a secret).

source.description: Step 33, shown by Subak: `config` (config.toml) or `detected` (found on this PC; never written).

secret_env.description: Shown by Subak (not in the file): the variables whose name or value looks secret.

default.description: Shown by Subak (not in the file): whether terminal.default_profile names it.
